It depends on what theory of time travel you believe in.

If you're in the multiple-universe camp, any change present self would make to past self would cause a whole new universe to be created with a new version of you. You would return to your time being yourself as you always had, the "new" version of you, essentially a completely different person, would reap the benefits. Present self would still exist in the shits.

If you're in the HG Wells camp, time is immutable and what happened in the past must happen or the future you will never have motivation to build a time-machine to travel back in time, a paradox cannot exist. No matter what you do or how many attempts you make to change the past, something will occur to correct your actions so that the past events inevitably unfold as they always had. Present self would still be in the shits.

Your only hope would be that a dynamic timeline is possible, where your future self can go back and make changes which will 'rewrite' all the future time ahead of your interaction with the past. But, you could go back and fuck something up terribly, possible making small changes which will ripple through time and create major changes - like accidentally killing your grandfather, creating a new Hitler, stepping on a bug that was a keystone to some evolutionary chain. There's no way to know what consequences could arise from even making a small intervention in past events. Present self would most likely still exist in the shit.

So, don't feel bad, friend! Focus on improving the future starting right this second. The past is in the past, and really should stay there.
